 494	// Both maps are read on every call regardless of scope. A group is only ever
 495	// written to one of them, so this cannot widen a grant; what it does is keep a
 496	// session grant honored by a request that forgot to set GroupSession.
 497	func (c *Coder) confirmGrouped(req ConfirmRequest) bool {
 498		if req.Group != "" && (c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] || c.sessionAutoApprove[req.Group]) {

 502		if res.Always && req.Group != "" {
 503			if req.GroupSession {
 504				c.sessionAutoApprove[req.Group] = true
 505			} else {
 506				c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] = true

 508		}

 512	// Run executes one scripted message (script mode) and returns the turn's
 513	// answer: every interrupted send's content in order, each steer as a
 514	// blockquote, and the final send's content — the same string the transcript
 515	// records.
 516	//
 517	// A panic inside the turn is recovered once, handed to OnCrash, and re-raised:
 518	// the transcript keeps the turn's partial answer (the caller appends its tool
 519	// lines and edited files from the same accessors it uses after a normal turn —
 520	// the panic unwound through runOne's defer, which settled those), and the
 521	// process still dies with the original stack trace. A recovered-and-swallowed
 522	// panic in a coding agent leaves the tree half-edited and the session running
 523	// on a broken coder; dying is the honest outcome. What recovery buys is that
 524	// the work the turn already did is not lost with the process.
 525	func (c *Coder) Run(ctx context.Context, withMessage string) (answer string) {
 526		defer func() {
 527			if r := recover(); r != nil {
 528				if c.OnCrash != nil {
 529					c.OnCrash(c.turnHistory + c.multiResponseContent + c.partialResponseContent)
 530				}
 531				panic(r)
 532			}
 533		}()
 534		c.runOne(ctx, withMessage)
 535		return c.turnHistory + c.multiResponseContent + c.partialResponseContent
 536	}

 538	// runOne is the turn loop. It keeps sending while the model has something to
 539	// react to — a tool result it hasn't seen (OutcomeContinue) or a mistake to fix
 540	// (OutcomeReflect) — and stops when the model has nothing left to say, the
 541	// human interrupts, or a budget is spent. The turn boundary is still the
 542	// human's: nothing here starts new work of its own.
 543	func (c *Coder) runOne(ctx context.Context, userMessage string) {
 544		c.initBeforeMessage()
 545		c.turnHistory = ""
 546	
 547		if userMessage == "" {
 548			return
 549		}
 550		message := userMessage
 551	
 552		// Committing and rotating settled history are both turn-end concerns.
 553		// Mid-loop the tool results must stay in cur, and summarizing them away
 554		// between steps would compact the very results the next send reacts to;
 555		// committing mid-loop would spend one commit per send on fragments of one
 556		// change. A defer covers every exit — budget declined, reflection cap,
 557		// interrupted, or done. An interrupted turn's edits are real, so they are
 558		// committed too.
 559		defer func() {
 560			c.settleEdits("")
 561			c.endTurnHistory()
 562			// Last, so the accounting closes the turn: the commit line above it, and
 563			// nothing under it. This is what the per-send reorder was reaching for,
 564			// now at the scope where a reader actually wants the number. Once per
 565			// turn even when the turn was steered, because a steered turn is still
 566			// one turn's spend.
 567			c.flushTurnUsage()
 568		}()
 569	
 570		// Outcome-driven so a re-send that carries no message text — both a tool
 571		// reflection and a tool continuation re-enter on the appended tool results
 572		// — keeps the loop going.
 573		for {
 574			outcome, reflection := c.sendSteerable(ctx, message)
 575			// After the send, not during it: sendMessage does its interrupt
 576			// handling before returning, and that handling can retract messages.
 577			c.recordNewMessages()
 578			c.lastSendOutcome = outcome
 579	
 580			switch outcome {
 581			case OutcomeReflect:
 582				if c.numReflections >= c.MaxErrorReflections {
 583					c.Out.Warningf("Only %d reflections allowed, stopping.", c.MaxErrorReflections)
 584					return
 585				}
 586				c.numReflections++
 587				message = reflection
 588	
 589			case OutcomeContinue:
 590				c.numSteps++
 591				if c.numSteps >= c.MaxSteps && !c.confirmMoreSteps() {
 592					return
 593				}
 594				message = "" // the tool results are the message
 595	
 596			case OutcomeSuccess:
 597				// The model has nothing more to call, so it believes it is done.
 598				// That is the moment to check, if the project asked us to.
 599				report, ok := c.runAutoCheck(ctx)
 600				if !ok {
 601					return
 602				}
 603				message = report
 604	
 605			case OutcomeInterrupted:
 606				next, keepGoing := c.afterInterrupt()
 607				if !keepGoing {
 608					return
 609				}
 610				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 611				message = next
 612	
 613			case OutcomeLooping:
 614				next, keepGoing := c.afterLoop()
 615				if !keepGoing {
 616					return
 617				}
 618				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 619				message = next
 620	
 621			default:
 622				return
 623			}
 624		}
 625	}

 627	// accumulateInterrupt saves the content of a send that was stopped before the
 628	// next send resets it, so the transcript can show the full arc of a steered
 629	// turn: what the model was saying, the steer, and the final answer.
 630	//
 631	// The steer is included when the user typed a custom correction rather than
 632	// choosing "Continue" (which carries no user text). A blockquote prefix makes
 633	// the authorship unambiguous in the markdown transcript.
 634	func (c *Coder) accumulateInterrupt(steer string) {
 635		if c.partialResponseContent != "" {
 636			c.turnHistory += c.partialResponseContent + "\n\n"
 637		}
 638		if steer != "" {
 639			c.turnHistory += "> " + strings.ReplaceAll(steer, "\n", "\n> ") + "\n\n"
 640		}
 641	}

 643	// sendSteerable runs one send under a context of its own, so that stopping the
 644	// send does not have to mean ending the turn.
 645	//
 646	// This is the whole of the change that makes steering possible. Ctrl-C used to
 647	// cancel the *turn's* context: everything downstream saw Canceled from then on,
 648	// and there was no way back into the loop even though the conversation itself
 649	// had survived intact. A child context per send moves the blast radius to the
 650	// one send, and the turn context stays live to make the next one.
 651	//
 652	// The tool calls of a send run inside it too — applyToolCalls takes this same
 653	// context — so Ctrl-C still kills a bash command that is running, which is the
 654	// property worth not losing.
 655	func (c *Coder) sendSteerable(ctx context.Context, message string) (SendOutcome, string) {
 656		sctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 657		c.sendMu.Lock()
 658		c.cancelSend = cancel
 659		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 660	
 661		defer func() {
 662			c.sendMu.Lock()
 663			c.cancelSend = nil
 664			c.sendMu.Unlock()
 665			cancel()
 666		}()
 667	
 668		return c.sendMessage(sctx, message)
 669	}

 671	// InterruptSend stops the send in flight without ending the turn.
 672	//
 673	// Called from the REPL's signal handler, which used to cancel the turn context
 674	// directly. A Ctrl-C between sends finds no send to cancel and does nothing,
 675	// which is correct: there is nothing in flight, and the prompt the user is
 676	// about to get asked is the interrupt they wanted.
 677	func (c *Coder) InterruptSend() {
 678		c.sendMu.Lock()
 679		cancel := c.cancelSend
 680		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 681		if cancel != nil {
 682			cancel()
 683		}
 684	}

 686	// settleEdits commits the turn's edits so far and records a snapshot to undo
 687	// them by.
 688	//
 689	// Factored out of the turn-end defer because an interruption is also a place
 690	// this belongs. The human stopped to look at something, which makes that point
 691	// a review boundary: `git show` gives exactly what the model did before it was
 692	// stopped, separately from what it did after the correction, and /undo steps
 693	// through the two halves one at a time. Anyone who wanted one commit has
 694	// /squash.
 695	//
 696	// What is *not* here is flushTurnUsage. The spend is a property of the turn,
 697	// not of each leg of it, so it stays in the defer and reports once.
 698	func (c *Coder) settleEdits(message string) {
 699		// Nothing written since the last settle, so there is nothing to settle.
 700		// Without this an interrupted-then-steered turn settles twice over the same
 701		// edits: the second commit finds the tree already matching HEAD and
 702		// announces "the turn left the files as they were", which is true of the
 703		// second attempt and false of the turn.
 704		//
 705		// turnSnap is the right signal rather than turnEditedFiles, which
 706		// accumulates across the whole turn because the history record at turn end
 707		// wants every file the turn touched. turnSnap is emptied by
 708		// pushTurnSnapshot and rebuilt by recordWrites, so it means precisely
 709		// "written since the last settle".
 710		if c.turnSnap.empty() {
 711			return
 712		}
 713		c.commitTurn(message)
 714		c.pushTurnSnapshot()
 715	}

 717	// afterInterrupt asks the human what a stopped turn should do next, and
 718	// reports the message to resume with and whether to resume at all.
 719	//
 720	// The choice is put through the Asker port, which is what ask_user_question
 721	// already uses to prompt in the middle of a turn — so this is a shape the
 722	// terminal handling has been driving all along rather than a new one. Free text
 723	// comes back as the raw line, which *is* the correction, so there is nothing to
 724	// parse. A nil Asker means no interactive terminal (script mode): stopping is
 725	// the only honest answer there, and it is what an interrupt has always done.
 726	//
 727	// The --yes flags deliberately do not answer this. They skip permission
 728	// prompts, and being asked what you meant by stopping is not a permission
 729	// prompt — the same line the port's own documentation draws for
 730	// ask_user_question.
 731	func (c *Coder) afterInterrupt() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 732		if c.Asker == nil {
 733			return "", false
 734		}
 735		// The edits so far belong to the interrupt, whichever way this goes.
 736		c.settleEdits("")
 737	
 738		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 739			Question: "You stopped the model. What now?",
 740			Options: []AskOption{
 741				{Label: "Continue", Description: "Carry on from where it was cut off"},
 742				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 743			},
 744		})
 745		if len(answer) == 0 {
 746			return "", false
 747		}
 748		switch answer[0] {
 749		case "Continue":
 750			// Say what the user decided, or the model is answering the wrong
 751			// question.
 752			//
 753			// noteInterrupt runs before this prompt, so all it can say is that the
 754			// reply was cut off. On its own that reads as a full stop, and the
 755			// model obliges: "No problem — I'll stop here. What would you like me
 756			// to do next?" It is not misreading anything. Asked afterwards what it
 757			// had been told, it quoted the cut-off note and said no continue choice
 758			// had reached it, which was exactly right.
 759			//
 760			// The rest of the wording closes the other failure mode. With a whole
 761			// partial reply above it and no instruction about what to do with it, a
 762			// model will also quite reasonably begin again from the top — which is
 763			// what an earlier live pass showed, and what was wrongly written up as
 764			// the cost of keeping the partial rather than as this bug.
 765			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 766				"The user chose to continue. Pick up exactly where your reply above "+
 767					"stops and carry on from there — do not start over, do not repeat "+
 768					"or summarize what you already wrote, and do not ask what to do next."))
 769			// The notes are the message, so the next send re-enters on them rather
 770			// than appending an empty user turn to carry nothing.
 771			c.resumeInPlace = true
 772			return "", true
 773		case "Stop":
 774			return "", false
 775		default:
 776			// Anything else the user typed is the steer, and it goes in as their
 777			// own words in their own voice. They really did type it.
 778			return answer[0], true
 779		}
 780	}

 782	// afterLoop asks what to do about a reply the harness stopped for repeating
 783	// itself, and reports whether the turn should continue.
 784	//
 785	// Its own function rather than a branch of afterInterrupt, because both halves
 786	// differ. The question cannot say "you stopped the model" — the user did not —
 787	// and "Continue" cannot mean "pick up exactly where your reply stops", which
 788	// here is an instruction to resume the loop. What is offered instead is a
 789	// retry: the loop's note (send.go) tells the model to take a different
 790	// approach, and the most useful thing the user can do is type what that should
 791	// be, which the free-text steer already carries.
 792	func (c *Coder) afterLoop() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 793		if c.Asker == nil {
 794			return "", false
 795		}
 796		// The edits so far belong to the stopped reply, whichever way this goes.
 797		c.settleEdits("")
 798	
 799		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 800			Question: "The model was repeating itself and was stopped. What now?",
 801			Options: []AskOption{
 802				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 803				{Label: "Try again", Description: "Let it answer again, told not to repeat itself"},
 804			},
 805		})
 806		if len(answer) == 0 {
 807			return "", false
 808		}
 809		switch answer[0] {
 810		case "Stop":
 811			return "", false
 812		case "Try again":
 813			// The note noteLoop already appended is the whole message: it says what
 814			// was stopped and what to do instead, so the next send re-enters on it
 815			// rather than appending an empty user turn to carry nothing.
 816			c.resumeInPlace = true
 817			return "", true
 818		default:
 819			// Anything else the user typed is the steer, in their own voice.
 820			return answer[0], true
 821		}
 822	}

 824	// runAutoCheck runs the project's check_auto checks at the end of a turn that
 825	// edited files, and reports whether the turn should continue.
 826	//
 827	// It fires here rather than after each edit because a mid-turn state is
 828	// legitimately broken: edit one file, then its caller, and in between nothing
 829	// compiles. Checking there would spend budget on failures the model was already
 830	// about to fix. At turn end the model has declared itself finished, which is
 831	// exactly when an independent check is worth something — and the reason to make
 832	// it independent is that the model's judgement about *which* check mattered is
 833	// the part that fails. A run that passed the tests and never linted still
 834	// reports "the checks pass".
 835	//
 836	// The returned message is a user turn, not a tool result, which is a deliberate
 837	// exception to the rule that reflection is a tool error. There is no call to
 838	// answer here: the model did not ask for this, the harness is speaking
 839	// unprompted, and a user message is the honest shape for that.
 840	func (c *Coder) runAutoCheck(ctx context.Context) (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 841		// Nothing changed since the last run — either the turn edited nothing at
 842		// all, or the model replied to a failure without touching a file, which is
 843		// a considered answer ("that isn't mine") and not something to re-ask.
 844		if len(c.CheckAuto) == 0 || !c.editedSinceCheck {
 845			return "", false
 846		}
 847		c.editedSinceCheck = false
 848		if c.autoChecks >= maxAutoCheck {
 849			c.Out.Warningf("The automatic checks have run %d times without passing; stopping here.", maxAutoCheck)
 850			return "", false
 851		}
 852		c.autoChecks++
 853	
 854		c.Out.Toolf("Running the automatic checks.")
 855		transcript, passed := c.runChecks(ctx, c.CheckAuto)
 856		if passed {
 857			return "", false
 858		}
 859		// The wording matters, and live testing is what showed why. "did not pass
 860		// after your changes" reads as "you caused this", which puts the model
 861		// between this message and the standing instruction to leave unrelated code
 862		// alone. Observed: it declined to fix a pre-existing failure, was asked
 863		// again by the next round, and gave in — two rounds spent on an argument the
 864		// harness started. Saying plainly that reporting is an acceptable answer
 865		// settles it in one.
 866		return "The automatic checks ran after your changes and did not pass:\n\n" + transcript +
 867			"\nIf this is something you broke, fix it. If it was already failing and is unrelated to " +
 868			"what you changed, say so and stop — don't fix it unless the user asks.", true
 869	}

 871	// confirmMoreSteps is the budget checkpoint. A long turn is legitimate, but it
 872	// should not run away unnoticed, so the user is shown what it has done so far
 873	// and asked whether to keep going. Declining ends the turn normally, with the
 874	// work up to that point already applied and committed. Answering yes buys
 875	// another MaxSteps.
 876	func (c *Coder) confirmMoreSteps() bool {
 877		files := len(c.turnEditedFiles)
 878		noun := "files"
 879		if files == 1 {
 880			noun = "file"
 881		}
 882		c.Out.Printf("This turn has run %d steps and edited %d %s.", c.numSteps, files, noun)
 883		if c.costKnown {
 884			c.Out.Printf("Cost so far: $%s.", formatCost(c.messageCost))
 885		}
 886	
 887		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(ConfirmRequest{Prompt: "Keep going?", Grant: GrantSteps})
 888		if !res.Yes {
 889			c.Out.Printf("Stopping here. The work so far is applied; say what to do next.")
 890			return false
 891		}
 892		c.numSteps = 0
 893		c.autoChecks = 0
 894		c.editedSinceCheck = false
 895		return true
 896	}

 943		}

 952	// StreamReasoning renders the model's thinking, plain.
 953	//
 954	// It used to be an empty function, so `strument -m … > transcript.txt` dropped
 955	// the whole reasoning trace without saying so, while the same session run
 956	// interactively showed it. Which mode you happened to use decided whether the
 957	// thinking existed — a decision nobody made, and one that cost several live
 958	// runs chasing a marker that could not appear. How much to show is now
 959	// reasoning_display's to answer, in both modes alike.
 960	func (o *StdOutput) StreamReasoning(delta string) {
 961		if o.think == nil {
 962			t := render.PlainThinking(os.Stdout, o.Thinking)
 963			// Pay the group separator at the opening marker: thinking opens lazily,
 964			// so a block that turns out to be empty never reaches Marker, and this
 965			// is the last point still above the "‹thinking›" the gap must precede.
 966			inner := t.Marker
 967			t.Marker = func(s string) {
 968				o.sep.Before(os.Stdout)
 969				o.streamed = true
 970				inner(s)
 971			}
 972			o.think = t
 973		}
 974		o.think.Write(render.Sanitize(delta))
 975	}

 979		if o.think == nil {
 980			return false
 981		}
 982		rendered := o.think.End()
 983		o.think = nil
 984		return rendered
 985	}

 987	func (o *StdOutput) StreamToolCall(index int, name, args string) {
 988		// Reasoning gave way to the calls it was about: no separator, since the
 989		// thinking heads this group. Clearing streamed by hand keeps the flush from
 990		// putting a blank directly above an outcome line printed by Toolf.
 991		if o.endReasoning() {
 992			o.streamed = false
 993		}

 154			case llm.EventToolCall:
 155				c.accumulateToolCall(ev.ToolCall)
 156				if ev.ToolCall != nil {
 157					c.Out.StreamToolCall(ev.ToolCall.Index, ev.ToolCall.Name, ev.ToolCall.Args)
 158				}
 159			case llm.EventFinish:
 160				finishReason = ev.FinishReason
 161			case llm.EventUsage:
 162				usage.add(ev.Usage)
 163			}
 164		}
 165		if finishReason == "length" {
 166			return resContinuation, nil
 167		}
 168		return resDone, nil
 169	}

 171	// retryBackoff carries the doubling delay for transient stream errors across a
 172	// send's retry loop.
 173	type retryBackoff struct{ delay time.Duration }
 174	
 175	// retry reports whether to retry a failed stream. A retryable error backs off —
 176	// doubling the delay (capped at retryTimeout) and sleeping — then returns true;
 177	// a non-retryable error, or one past the cap, reports the failure and returns
 178	// false. It takes Output and Clock rather than the Coder so the side-model
 179	// side calls (side.go) share it without owning one; sendMessage, RunAside, and
 180	// those side calls all retry identically.
 181	func (rb *retryBackoff) retry(out Output, clock Clock, streamErr error) bool {
 182		var se *llm.StreamError
 183		if !errors.As(streamErr, &se) || !se.Retryable() {
 184			out.Errorf("%v", streamErr)
 185			return false
 186		}
 187		rb.delay *= 2
 188		if rb.delay > retryTimeout {
 189			out.Errorf("%s", se.Error())
 190			return false
 191		}
 192		out.Warningf("%s", se.Error())
 193		out.Printf("Retrying in %.1f seconds...", rb.delay.Seconds())
 194		clock.Sleep(rb.delay)
 195		return true
 196	}

 198	// sendMessage is the phase machine. It returns the outcome and, for
 199	// OutcomeReflect, the next message to send.
 200	func (c *Coder) sendMessage(ctx context.Context, inp string) (SendOutcome, string) {
 201		// --- Setup ---
 202		// A resumed send re-enters on what is already in curMessages — tool
 203		// results, or an interrupted reply the user chose to continue — so it adds
 204		// no user turn; inp is unused on that path.
 205		appendedUser := false
 206		if c.resumeInPlace {
 207			c.resumeInPlace = false
 208		} else {
 209			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.TextMessage("user", inp))
 210			appendedUser = true
 211		}
 212	
 213		chunks := c.formatMessages()
 214		messages := chunks.allMessages()
 215	
 216		if !c.checkTokens(messages) {
 217			if appendedUser {
 218				c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:len(c.curMessages)-1]
 219			}
 220			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 221		}
 222	
 223		// --- Stream ---
 224		c.multiResponseContent = "" // per-send reset (H1)
 225	
 226		usage := &sendUsage{estSent: c.countMessages(messages) + c.countTools()}
 227		defer c.finalizeUsage(usage)
 228	
 229		backoff := retryBackoff{delay: initialRetryDelay}
 230		continuations := 0
 231	
 232		// One detector per send, not per streamOnce: a continuation is the same
 233		// reply resumed, and a loop that spans the stitch is still a loop.
 234		loops := newLoopDetector(c.LoopDetection)
 235	
 236		// term is how the whole stream phase ended, as opposed to how one
 237		// streamOnce ended: retries and continuations loop without setting it.
 238		// streamOnce already classifies precisely, so the phase carries that
 239		// classification forward rather than re-encoding it into flags. Every path
 240		// out of the loop below assigns it before breaking.
 241		var term streamResult
 242	
 243		for {
 244			c.partialResponseContent = ""
 245			c.partialReasoningContent = ""
 246			c.partialToolCalls = nil
 247			c.toolCallIndex = map[int]int{}
 248	
 249			res, streamErr := c.streamOnce(ctx, c.buildRequest(messages), usage, loops)
 250	
 251			if res == resFailed {
 252				// A retryable error backs off and retries (the partial is discarded
 253				// at the loop top; accumulated multiResponseContent is untouched);
 254				// anything else is a hard failure.
 255				if backoff.retry(c.Out, c.Clock, streamErr) {
 256					continue
 257				}
 258				term = resFailed
 259				break
 260			}
 261	
 262			if res == resContinuation {
 263				if !c.PrefillSupported {
 264					term = resOutputExhausted
 265					break
 266				}
 267				continuations++
 268				if continuations > continuationCap {
 269					term = resOutputExhausted // cap hit
 270					break
 271				}
 272				// Stitch: accumulated + current partial becomes the prefill.
 273				c.multiResponseContent += c.partialResponseContent
 274				if n := len(messages); n > 0 && messages[n-1].Role == "assistant" {
 275					messages[n-1] = llm.TextMessage("assistant", c.multiResponseContent)
 276				} else {
 277					messages = append(messages, llm.TextMessage("assistant", c.multiResponseContent))
 278				}
 279				continue
 280			}
 281	
 282			term = res // resDone, resInterrupted, resLooping, resContextExhausted
 283			break
 284		}
 285		interrupted := term == resInterrupted
 286	
 287		// --- Finally (always runs) ---
 288		c.Out.FlushStream()
 289		answer := c.multiResponseContent + c.partialResponseContent
 290		answer = stripReasoning(answer, c.Model.ReasoningTag)
 291		c.partialResponseContent = answer
 292		c.multiResponseContent = ""
 293	
 294		// --- Post-stream dispatch ---
 295		c.finalizeUsage(usage)
 296	
 297		if answer != "" || len(c.partialToolCalls) > 0 {
 298			msg := llm.TextMessage("assistant", answer)
 299			if len(c.partialToolCalls) > 0 {
 300				msg.ToolCalls = c.partialToolCalls
 301			}
 302			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, msg)
 303		}
 304	
 305		// dropUserTurn un-appends the user message this send added, so a send that
 306		// produced nothing doesn't poison the history. It is a no-op on a tool
 307		// continuation, which appended no user turn — truncating there would drop a
 308		// tool result and leave a tool_call unanswered, making the next request
 309		// malformed.
 310		dropUserTurn := func() {
 311			if appendedUser {
 312				c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:len(c.curMessages)-1]
 313			}
 314		}
 315	
 316		switch term {
 317		case resContextExhausted:
 318			// A system message, not an assistant one. The model did not say this —
 319			// the request never reached a reply — so putting it in the assistant's
 320			// voice fabricates a turn, and one in which the model appears to report
 321			// its own transport error. The note exists so the next request does not
 322			// end on a bare user turn with no answer, which is what the role check
 323			// below is for; whose voice carries it is a separate question, and the
 324			// harness's own is the honest one.
 325			if n := len(c.curMessages); n > 0 && c.curMessages[n-1].Role == "user" {
 326				c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages,
 327					llm.TextMessage(llm.RoleSystem, "The reply was cut off: the request exceeded the context limit."))
 328			}
 329			c.showExhaustedError()
 330			return OutcomeContextExhausted, ""
 331		case resOutputExhausted:
 332			// The large partial was kept above; no diagnostic (trailing message
 333			// is the assistant partial).
 334			return OutcomeOutputExhausted, ""
 335		case resFailed:
 336			if answer == "" {
 337				dropUserTurn()
 338			}
 339			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 340		case resLooping:
 341			// The user turn stays. Unlike an empty reply, this one produced
 342			// something — it produced too much of one thing — and the note below
 343			// only makes sense following the message it answers.
 344			c.warnLoop(loops.Found)
 345			c.noteLoop(loops.Found)
 346			return OutcomeLooping, ""
 347		}
 348	
 349		if !interrupted && answer == "" && len(c.partialToolCalls) == 0 {
 350			dropUserTurn()
 351			c.Out.Warningf("Empty response received from LLM. Check your provider account?")
 352			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 353		}
 354	
 355		if interrupted {
 356			c.noteInterrupt()
 357			return OutcomeInterrupted, ""
 358		}
 359	
 360		// Everything a turn does now arrives as tool calls, in every mode: ask mode
 361		// is the same dispatch with the mutating tools withheld. There is no longer
 362		// a second path that reads the answer text for edits, shell blocks, or file
 363		// mentions — those were the text formats' way of saying what a tool call
 364		// says directly.
 365		return c.applyToolCalls(ctx), ""
 366	}

 368	// noteInterrupt records that the human stopped the reply, in a shape the next
 369	// request can be built from.
 370	//
 371	// Two things it deliberately does not do, both of which it used to.
 372	//
 373	// It does not put words in the model's mouth. The old shape appended an
 374	// assistant turn saying "I see that you interrupted my previous reply", which
 375	// the model never said; the harness's own voice is the honest one, and the rest
 376	// of this file already says so about the context-exhausted note.
 377	//
 378	// It does not edit "^C KeyboardInterrupt" into the user's own message. Whatever
 379	// the human typed is what the human typed. assemble.go makes the same argument
 380	// about the system reminder, and this was the last place still doing it.
 381	//
 382	// The partial reply itself stays. It is real output the model produced, and
 383	// keeping it is what makes "continue as before" continue rather than restart.
 384	// Its *tool calls* do not stay — see dropPartialToolCalls.
 385	func (c *Coder) noteInterrupt() {
 386		c.dropPartialToolCalls()
 387		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 388			"The user pressed Ctrl-C, so your reply above was cut off where it stops. "+
 389				"Anything you were part-way through saying was not finished, and any tool "+
 390				"call you had begun was not run — nothing it would have changed has changed."))
 391	}

 393	// warnLoop tells the user what the model was doing when it was stopped, in
 394	// every mode: script runs have no steer menu, and a run that stopped early is
 395	// the one thing a log must not be silent about.
 396	func (c *Coder) warnLoop(f *loopFinding) {
 397		if f == nil {
 398			c.Out.Warningf("The model's reply was repeating itself, so it was stopped.")
 399			return
 400		}
 401		c.Out.Warningf("The model's %s was repeating itself (%q %d times), so it was stopped.",
 402			f.Kind, f.Sample, f.Count)
 403	}

 405	// noteLoop records that the harness stopped a reply that was repeating itself.
 406	//
 407	// In the harness's own voice, for the same reason as noteInterrupt: nobody
 408	// pressed Ctrl-C, and saying the user did would be a fabrication about the one
 409	// participant whose actions the model cannot check.
 410	//
 411	// It quotes the repeating text back. A model given "you were repeating
 412	// yourself" and nothing else has to guess which part, and the guess is often
 413	// the whole reply; the sample makes the instruction actionable.
 414	func (c *Coder) noteLoop(f *loopFinding) {
 415		c.dropPartialToolCalls()
 416		where := "reply"
 417		if f != nil && f.Kind == loopReasoning {
 418			where = "reasoning"
 419		}
 420		note := "Strument stopped your " + where + " because it had begun repeating itself"
 421		if f != nil {
 422			note += fmt.Sprintf(" — %q appeared %d times", f.Sample, f.Count)
 423		}
 424		note += ". Nothing you were part-way through was finished, and any tool call " +
 425			"you had begun was not run. Do not continue that text or write it again: " +
 426			"take a different approach, and if you are stuck, say so plainly and stop."
 427		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(note))
 428	}

 430	// noteToolInterrupt records a Ctrl-C that landed while a tool was running.
 431	//
 432	// Distinct from noteInterrupt, which describes a *stream* cut off mid-word and
 433	// says any tool call the model had begun was never run. Here the opposite is
 434	// true: the calls ran, their results are in the history, and one of them was
 435	// stopped part-way. Telling the model the other story would have it repeat work
 436	// that already happened, or distrust a result that is real.
 437	func (c *Coder) noteToolInterrupt() {
 438		c.partialToolCalls = nil
 439		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 440			"The user pressed Ctrl-C while your tool calls were running. Their results "+
 441				"above are real as far as they got, and a command that was stopped says so "+
 442				"in its own output. Nothing after the interruption ran."))
 443	}

 445	// dropPartialToolCalls strips tool calls from the assistant message an
 446	// interrupted send just appended.
 447	//
 448	// Not tidiness — correctness. An unanswered tool_call makes the *next* request
 449	// malformed, and after an interrupt no result will ever answer one: the call is
 450	// either half-streamed and unparseable, or complete but never dispatched,
 451	// because the interrupt landed before applyToolCalls ran. Either way the model
 452	// must be told it did not happen, which the note above does, rather than shown
 453	// a call it may assume succeeded.
 454	//
 455	// The message's text survives. Only an assistant message can carry tool calls,
 456	// so this looks at one message and only when it is the last.
 457	func (c *Coder) dropPartialToolCalls() {
 458		c.partialToolCalls = nil
 459		n := len(c.curMessages)
 460		if n == 0 {
 461			return
 462		}
 463		last := &c.curMessages[n-1]
 464		if last.Role != llm.RoleAssistant || len(last.ToolCalls) == 0 {
 465			return
 466		}
 467		if last.Text() == "" {
 468			// Nothing but the abandoned calls: drop the whole turn rather than
 469			// leave an empty assistant message in the history.
 470			c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:n-1]
 471			return
 472		}
 473		last.ToolCalls = nil
 474	}

 476	// buildRequest translates state into an llm.Request.
 477	func (c *Coder) buildRequest(messages []llm.Message) llm.Request {
 478		req := llm.Request{
 479			Model:           c.Model.Slug,
 480			Messages:        messages,
 481			Temperature:     c.Model.Temperature,
 482			ReasoningEffort: c.Model.Reasoning,
 483			ExtraParams:     c.Model.RequestExtraParams(),
 484		}
 485		// Whatever tools this mode offers, offer them. The condition used to be
 486		// editFormat == "tool", which meant ask mode sent none at all — and made
 487		// toolDefs's own "ask" branch unreachable, so the code read as though ask
 488		// had a read-only tool set while the wire carried nothing. A model told to
 489		// look at the project with no way to do it invents the syntax: MiMo emitted
 490		// <bash>ls -la</bash> as prose, and one run spent 759 lines guessing at
 491		// markup. RunAside builds its own request and is deliberately not affected.
 492		if defs := c.toolDefs(); len(defs) > 0 {
 493			req.Tools = defs
 494			req.ToolChoice = "auto"
 495		}
 496		return req
 497	}

 499	// CheckRestoredContext warns if what a session *starts* with already overruns
 500	// the declared window.
 501	//
 502	// Restored context is invisible until the first request, and by then the request
 503	// has failed. aider #2979 is the shape: an 80k-token restored history fails on
 504	// the wire, and configuring the side model for summarization does not help,
 505	// because compaction runs at the end of a turn and there has not been one yet.
 506	// Strument restores less — pins, notes, and the read-only block rather than a
 507	// conversation — but the same trap is available, and a user who pinned a large
 508	// spec last session should hear about it before typing rather than after.
 509	//
 510	// It warns rather than asking. A confirmation before the user has typed
 511	// anything is a toll on every start, and there is nothing to decide yet: the
 512	// remedy is /drop or /notes drop, which they can reach either way.
 513	func (c *Coder) CheckRestoredContext() {
 514		if c.Model == nil || c.Model.Context <= 0 {
 515			return
 516		}
 517		n := c.countMessages(c.formatMessages().allMessages()) + c.countTools()
 518		if n < c.Model.Context {
 519			return
 520		}
 521		c.Out.Warningf("This session starts with about %d tokens of context, which already reaches "+
 522			"the %d-token limit for %s.", n, c.Model.Context, c.Model.QualifiedSlug())
 523		c.Out.Printf("Use /drop to unpin files, /notes drop to discard the session notes, or /tokens to see the split.")
 524	}

 526	// checkTokens warns when the estimate reaches the input window and asks to
 527	// proceed.
 528	func (c *Coder) checkTokens(messages []llm.Message) bool {
 529		maxInput := c.Model.Context
 530		if maxInput <= 0 {
 531			return true
 532		}
 533		// The schemas count: they go out with this request like everything else,
 534		// and leaving them out made the guard cheerful about a prompt 1.3k tokens
 535		// closer to the limit than it reported.
 536		inputTokens := c.countMessages(messages) + c.countTools()
 537		if inputTokens < maxInput {
 538			return true
 539		}
 540		c.Out.Errorf("Your estimated chat context of %d tokens exceeds the %d token limit for %s!",
 541			inputTokens, maxInput, c.Model.QualifiedSlug())
 542		c.Out.Printf("To reduce the chat context:")
 543		c.Out.Printf("- Use /drop to remove unneeded files from the chat")
 544		c.Out.Printf("- Use /clear to clear the chat history")
 545		c.Out.Printf("- Break your code into smaller files")
 546		c.Out.Printf("It's probably safe to try and send the request, most providers won't charge if the context limit is exceeded.")
 547		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(ConfirmRequest{Prompt: "Try to proceed anyway?", Grant: GrantContext})
 548		return res.Yes

 551	// moveBackCurMessages rotates cur into done on edited turns.
 552	//
 553	// aider appended a synthetic "I applied and committed your changes" user turn
 554	// here, plus an "Ok." from the assistant, because with SEARCH/REPLACE there was
 555	// no other channel: a text edit format has nothing to answer the model with.
 556	// The tool loop has one. Every edit call already gets a tool result saying what
 557	// it did to which file, so the pair would only repeat it — two fabricated
 558	// messages per turn, in a loop whose whole correction was to stop inventing
 559	// turns the model never took. The commit is reported to the user instead, where
 560	// the hash is worth something.
 561	func (c *Coder) moveBackCurMessages() {
 562		c.doneMessages = append(c.doneMessages, c.curMessages...)
 563		c.curMessages = nil
 564		c.recordedMessages = 0
 565		c.maybeSummarize()
 566	}

 568	// endTurnHistory settles the finished turn and compacts if it has outgrown the
 569	// budget. Called once from runOne's defer, after the commit and the snapshot.
 570	//
 571	// It used to be gated on `editFormat == "tool" && len(turnEditedFiles) > 0`, so
 572	// only a turn that changed a file produced any settled history at all. A live
 573	// pass found what that costs: a session of questions, or any stretch of /ask,
 574	// kept everything in curMessages — which goes on the wire in full and which
 575	// maybeSummarize never examines — so the history budget existed and nothing was
 576	// ever measured against it.
 577	//
 578	// The gate is a vestige. In aider the rotation carried a synthetic "I applied
 579	// and committed your changes" pair, which only made sense after an edit;
 580	// moveBackCurMessages's own comment records removing the pair, and the gate
 581	// stayed behind. What genuinely must not happen is rotating *mid-loop*, where
 582	// compaction would eat the tool results the next send reacts to — and that is
 583	// enforced by this running in the turn-end defer, not by asking what the turn
 584	// did.
 585	//
 586	// Rotation does not move anything on the wire: done and cur are adjacent and
 587	// both sit after the read-only block, so the split is bookkeeping. What changes
 588	// is that compaction can now see the conversation.
 589	func (c *Coder) endTurnHistory() {
 590		if len(c.curMessages) == 0 {
 591			return
 592		}
 593		c.moveBackCurMessages()
 594	}

 597	// derived from the main model's window, with a 2048 floor for small windows.
 598	// It is increased from aider's context/16.

 600		return max(context/8, 2048)

 603	// countSummaryMessages reports how many retained history messages are compaction summaries.
 604	func countSummaryMessages(msgs []llm.Message) int {
 605		n := 0
 606		for _, m := range msgs {
 607			if isSummaryMessage(m) {
 608				n++
 609			}
 610		}

 614	func validCompaction(msgs []llm.Message, beforeTokens, beforeMessages, afterTokens int) bool {
 615		return len(msgs) < beforeMessages && afterTokens < beforeTokens && hasSummaryContent(msgs)
 616	}

 618	func hasSummaryContent(msgs []llm.Message) bool {
 619		for _, m := range msgs {
 620			if isSummaryMessage(m) && strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(m.Text(), summaryPrefix)) != "" {
 621				return true
 622			}
 623		}
 624		return false
 625	}

 627	// budget. It runs only when a summarizer is wired and the model's window is
 628	// known (Context > 0) — mirroring checkTokens, which treats an unknown window
 629	// as "no limit to enforce". Synchronous: the side-model call happens here,
 630	// before the next prompt is assembled. On failure the history is left intact.
 631	func (c *Coder) maybeSummarize() {
 632		if c.Summarizer == nil || c.Model.Context <= 0 {
 633			return
 634		}
 635		budget := maxChatHistoryTokens(c.Model.Context)
 636		if !c.Summarizer.tooBig(c.doneMessages, budget) {
 637			return
 638		}
 639		if c.summaryBackoff {
 640			c.summaryBackoff = false
 641			return
 642		}
 643		c.Out.Printf("Summarizing chat history to fit the context window...")
 644		beforeTokens := c.Summarizer.total(c.doneMessages)
 645		beforeMessages := len(c.doneMessages)
 646		out, err := c.Summarizer.summarize(c.doneMessages, budget)
 647		if err != nil {
 648			c.summaryBackoff = true
 649			c.Out.Warningf("Could not summarize chat history: %v", err)
 650			return
 651		}
 652		afterTokens := c.Summarizer.total(out)
 653		if !validCompaction(out, beforeTokens, beforeMessages, afterTokens) {
 654			c.summaryBackoff = true
 655			c.Out.Warningf("Could not summarize chat history: the result was not smaller than the original history")
 656			return
 657		}
 658		c.doneMessages = out
 659		c.Out.Printf("Chat history compacted: %d tokens/%s -> %d tokens/%s; %s retained.",
 660			beforeTokens, plural(beforeMessages, "message", "messages"),
 661			afterTokens, plural(len(out), "message", "messages"),
 662			plural(countSummaryMessages(out), "summary", "summaries"))
 663	}

 665	// finalizeUsage resolves cost — (1) in-band cost, (2) config
 666	// pricing, (3) tokens only, never a fabricated $0 — merges into session
 667	// totals, and emits the immutable report. Idempotent; also deferred so a
 668	// mid-send panic can't lose accounting.
 669	func (c *Coder) finalizeUsage(u *sendUsage) {
 670		if u.finalized {
 671			return
 672		}
 673		u.finalized = true
 674	
 675		// prompt_tokens is the whole prompt. Both cache figures live under
 676		// prompt_tokens_details and are a *breakdown* of it, not additions to it:
 677		// on a cold request with a breakpoint, OpenRouter returns
 678		// prompt_tokens=14021, cache_write_tokens=14018, and
 679		// total_tokens=14026 = prompt + completion. Adding the write on top counted
 680		// most of the prompt twice, and only on models that write a cache — which
 681		// is why GPT-5.6 Luna looked like it was sending an order of magnitude more
 682		// than Haiku for the same work. Cache reads were already treated as the
 683		// subset they are; the two are the same kind of number.
 684		sent := u.prompt
 685		received := u.completion
 686		estimated := false
 687	
 688		// A request the provider refused outright — a bad key, a model slug that
 689		// does not exist, an account out of credit — was not processed: no usage,
 690		// no reply, nothing billed. Estimating it printed
 691		//
 692		//	Tokens: 735 sent, 0 received. (estimated)
 693		//
 694		// under a 401, which reads as a charge for the failure. Returning before
 695		// the counters means messageSends stays 0 and flushTurnUsage says nothing
 696		// at all, which is the honest report.
 697		//
 698		// A stream that produced text before it broke is a different case: those
 699		// tokens were generated and will be billed, so it still estimates below.
 700		if u.rejected && sent == 0 && received == 0 && !u.costKnown && c.streamedText() == "" {
 701			return
 702		}
